# 📐 Editorial Production Standard, Monthly Content Engine & Brand Direction — WN × LIQ9 (v2, standing)

Source page: https://app.notion.com/p/3729d75ae4b581a883ddc176804fdbdd
Parent: 2026 WNLQ9 — Content Hub (35e9d75a-e4b5-809f-9f9c-cfdbb9b95e6d)
Captured: 2026-06-03 via notion-fetch (enhanced markdown).

> Read this before writing or editing any piece. This is a standing standard (v2) — it governs every monthly slate, not one month. Each month's rows live in that month's `YYYY MON — WNLQ9 — Content Production` database and must be written to this standard and pass the Editorial Council Checklist (§12) before Status moves Review → Done. If the copy could have been written by any wine/spirits retailer in the world, it does not pass.
>
> How to read this doc: §§1–14 = the per-piece writing/quality standard. §15 = the Monthly Content Engine (the repeatable workflow for building a whole month). §16–17 = Brand Direction per site. §18 = cross-brand + platform rules (incl. the Magento no-emoji rule). Proven on June 2026 (~86 rows) and July 2026 (80 rows).

## 1. How the brief works
Each calendar row carries a 📋 Production Brief (strategy + structure) and, for Heroes, a ✍️ Ready-to-Write Spec (section-by-section build). Structured fields (Author, Word Target, Intent, Funnel, Schema, Evergreen, Priority) live in the database properties. Writer fills the draft into Content TH / Content EN; editor runs §12 before publish.

## 2. The two voices (non-negotiable)
### 🍷 Wine-Now — Bangkok's sommelier, in your pocket
- Magazine tone, Thai-first, warm, knowledgeable, never academic. English for connoisseur/expat/product notes.
- No hyperbole. "Albariño for a 35-degree Bangkok afternoon," never "a great wine."
- Never "drink this" — always why this bottle, this moment, this table.
- We say no (a sommelier who recommends everything recommends nothing), we explain (story not spec sheet), we remember (LINE OA), we're Thai.
- NOT a supermarket, NOT a wine school, NOT "premium for status." Premium = quality + fit.
### 🥃 LIQ9 — the spirits intelligence behind Bangkok's bar scene
- Voice = Master-of-Malt wit + Bangkok-bartender confidence. Short-sentence confidence, em-dash rhythm, insider language, self-aware humor. Earn the exclamation mark (use fewer than WN).
- Decode, don't lecture. Context (the cocktail, the culture) before the product/bottle name.
- Cocktail-culture lens always present — even a sipping whisky gets a highball note.
- Name real Bangkok bars / bartenders wherever possible.
- NOT Wishbeer (they list, we curate), NOT a duty-free, NOT an importer, NOT whisky-only.
### Universal rule (both)
> Every piece should leave the reader feeling they got advice from a brilliant, knowledgeable friend — not a salesperson, professor, or algorithm.

## 3. Author & E-E-A-T policy
- Each piece gets an Author (property): Wine-Now Sommelier Desk, LIQ9 Bartender Desk, or Guest Expert.
- A real, named, credentialed human must stand behind every byline (WSET/sommelier cert for WN; bartender/industry credential for LIQ9). Do not invent personas — Google penalises fabricated expertise and it breaks trust.
- Every published page needs an author bio + photo + credentials and Person/author schema. First-person experience ("we tasted," "we tested") is encouraged and is the strongest E-E-A-T signal.

## 4. Brief anatomy (what every row must contain)
1. Meta title (≤60 char, keyword near front) · Meta description (≤160, benefit + CTA)
2. Primary keyword + 3–5 secondaries (TH + EN)
3. Intent (Informational/Commercial/Transactional) · Funnel (TOFU/MOFU/BOFU)
4. Word Target (see §5) · Type · Priority · Evergreen/Timely
5. Direct-answer block (40–60 words, see §6)
6. H2/H3 structure with a one-line angle per section + per-section word budget
7. FAQ (3–5 Q with answer direction)
8. Internal links (3–5, hub-and-spoke) + external authority links
9. Sourcing plan (which Tier-1–3 sources, which scores) — §8
10. Image shot list (hero 1200×630 + alt; inline graphics/product) — §7
11. CTA (compliance-safe — §9) + product widgets
12. Schema types (§7)

## 5. Content types & length (house spec)
| Type | Word target | Prime publish slot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pillar | 2,500 | Mon 08:00 |
| Spoke / Blog | 1,200 | Tue–Fri 08:00 |
| Basic / Tips / Pairing / Rec / Life | 800 | 10:00 |
| Filler (snackable explainer) | 600–800 | flexible / weekend |

> June cadence note: the June slate runs an elevated ~2–3 posts/day incl. weekends (74 pieces). Use Priority to allocate effort: Hero = full depth, prime weekday slot, full promotion; Standard = solid; Filler = lean, can take weekend/low slots. Don't spread a team thin pretending every piece is a Hero.

## 6. SEO & GEO (AI-search) requirements
- Direct-answer block opens every piece: 40–60 words that answer the query outright (wins AI Overviews / ChatGPT / Perplexity citations). State the verdict, then justify below.
- Primary keyword in: H1, first 100 words, one H2, meta title, URL slug, one image alt.
- Hub-and-spoke internal linking: every spoke links up to its pillar; pillar links down to ≥3 spokes. Use descriptive anchors, not "click here."
- Schema (JSON-LD) by page type: Article + FAQPage (all); Product+Review (brand/PDP); ItemList (listicles/collections); BreadcrumbList (all); Person (author).
- Passage-level structure: short paragraphs, descriptive H2/H3 phrased as real questions where possible.

## 7. Imagery standard
- Hero 1200×630 (OG-safe), descriptive Thai alt text with primary keyword.
- At least one original inline asset (comparison table / flavor map / recipe card) — reuse house templates (one sweetness/body chart, one tannin scale, one flavor map) rather than bespoke each time.
- Product shots route to widgets; never show pricing on-image (§9).

## 8. Sourcing standard (non-negotiable)
- No self-invented scores. Every score/tasting note traces to a named source. If none exists, label it "house description."
- Tier 1 producer/distillery/Comité official notes · Tier 2 named critics & competitions · Tier 3 market/auction data.
- Wine (WN): Decanter, James Suckling, Vinous, Wine Spectator, Robert Parker, Burghound, Wine-Searcher (market).
- Spirits (LIQ9): Whisky Advocate, Jim Murray's Whisky Bible, Serge Valentin/Whiskyfun, Difford's Guide, IWSC/SFWSC, World Whiskies Awards.
- Attribute inline ("Decanter, 97 pts"). Cross-reference a second source for any 95+ / investment claim.

## 9. 🇹🇭 Thai compliance gate (hard gate — cannot publish without)
Thailand's Alcohol Beverage Control Act B.E. 2551 restricts alcohol advertising. For every commercial/brand/price/buy piece:
- No on-page pricing; use "price-on-request / order via LINE @."
- No consumption-inducing language or claims of superiority that induce drinking.
- No direct on-page "buy" CTA; route to LINE OA / catalogue.
- Age-gate / 20+ responsible-drinking note where applicable.
- Check the publish date against Buddhist holy days (alcohol sales bans); on those days run education-only, no product (cf. LIQ9 "VIS" type).
- Rows carrying ⚠️ in-body need legal sign-off before Status → Done.

## 10. Localization
TH and EN are two native voices, not a translation. Write TH for Thai search nuance and culture; EN for connoisseur/expat. Keep keyword intent in both. No machine-flipped copy.

## 11. Promotion / margin rules (LIQ9 + WN)
- No blanket % off on low-margin SKUs. Bestsellers (5–15% margin): bundle / GWP / free-shipping threshold only. Higher-margin lines (e.g. Iron Balls Gin ~32%): direct discount/bundle OK.
- WN: walk away from price-led promotions that train customers to wait for discounts; no SKUs <฿800 that don't serve progression.

## 12. ✅ Editorial Council acceptance checklist (the gate)
A piece passes to Done/Published only if ALL are true:
- [ ] Voice unmistakably WN or LIQ9 (§2) — couldn't have been written by any retailer
- [ ] Direct-answer block present (40–60w) and accurate
- [ ] Hits Word Target for its Type; structure matches brief
- [ ] Primary keyword placement complete; 3–5 internal links (hub-spoke) live
- [ ] Every score/claim sourced (Tier 1–3) or marked "house description" — zero fabricated facts
- [ ] FAQ (3–5) + required schema implemented
- [ ] Hero image 1200×630 + Thai alt; ≥1 original inline asset
- [ ] Thai compliance gate passed (§9) + legal sign-off if ⚠️
- [ ] TH & EN both native-quality (§10)
- [ ] Named author + bio + credentials + author schema (§3)
- [ ] Compliance-safe CTA + correct product widgets
- [ ] Repurposing assets handed off (§13)

## 13. Repurposing / atomization (do more with less)
Every Hero ships a content tree, not just an article:
- 3–5 social cut-downs (IG/FB/TikTok) — one stat, one tip, one myth, one product, one quote
- 1 email feature for the LINE OA / newsletter
- 1 short-video script (30–45s) for the strongest hook (esp. the "we tested" pieces)
- Pillars seed their spokes' social too. Log assets in the row before §12 sign-off.

## 14. Definition of Done
Draft (TH+EN) in Content fields → editor runs §12 → legal sign-off where ⚠️ → schema + images attached → repurpose tree logged → Status: Done → schedule to Publish Date/slot → Published + Final URL filled.

# PART B — THE MONTHLY CONTENT ENGINE
## 15. How we design & develop a month (repeatable workflow)
Run the steps in order. Do not skip Step 1 (research) or the two council passes (Steps 3 and 5).
### 15.1 Step 0 — Lock the month's parameters
- Volume & cadence — Full engine (~80 rows, 2–3 posts/day) · Lean & focused (~40) · Mid (~55–60).
- Evidence basis — validate with live keyword/SERP/trend data, or plan from editorial judgment.
- Focus anchor — a campaign/sale window, a seasonal theme, or a balanced editorial month.
### 15.2 Step 1 — Live-signal research (always before topic design)
Pull and record these, tagging anything factual as [VERIFY]:
- Drinks calendar — international/national drink days (WSET 2026 drinks calendar, Master of Malt calendar). e.g. World Rum Day, Bastille Day, Tequila Day, Scotch Day.
- Thai seasonal & cultural context — rainy season, festivals, gifting moments.
- Thai alcohol SALES-BAN dates (hard compliance pin) — the 5 Buddhist holy days: Makha Bucha, Visakha Bucha, Asalha Bucha, Khao Phansa (start of Lent), Ok Phansa. These shift each year — confirm exact dates every month. Pin them to the calendar before anything else.
- E-commerce windows — mid-year 7.7, 9.9, 11.11, 12.12, etc. (handle per the naming rule in §15.6).
- Pin timely/dated pieces first; evergreen content fills around them.
### 15.3 Step 2 — Cluster architecture (hub-and-spoke)
- Design 6–8 topic clusters for the month. Each cluster = 1 Pillar hub + 4–8 Blog/Social spokes.
- Anchor each cluster to a date (timely) or an evergreen need.
- Cross-month linking: new hubs link back to prior-month pillars (e.g. July's Tequila links to June's Mezcal). Spokes always link up to their hub.
- Balance: ~50/50 Wine-Now / LIQ9 · ~2–3 posts/day · never two similar pieces adjacent · weekends lighter.
- Priority tiers: Hero (pillars + big timely) ~15% · Standard (blogs) ~55% · Filler (social) ~30%.
### 15.4 Step 3 — Council pre-flight (review the PLAN, before writing)
Run the §12 panel on the plan — titles, angles, dates, cluster map — not just finished drafts. This catches compliance, duplication, and voice problems at the cheapest stage. Get owner sign-off on the calendar and any topic swaps before building.
### 15.5 Step 4 — Build the month
- A new month = a new sibling database named `YYYY MON — WNLQ9 — Content Production`, created under the 2026 Content Calendar Hub, mirroring the schema exactly; add that month's option to the Month select.
- Create rows in batches of 6–8 with full metadata + Content Brief + KEY/STORY/TENSION + bilingual DRAFT v1, Status = Review.
- DRAFT v1 = direct-answer skeleton (direct answer 40–60w → section build → FAQ → CTA, in TH and EN). It is intentionally not the final word-count article. Hero expansion to full length is a separate, explicit step (§15.8).
### 15.6 Compliance rules that bite every month (extends §9)
- Sale events — never name or sell the sale. Do not use a sale name ("7.7", "11.11") or the words buy / cart / shopping list / stock up / % off in any title, body, or social caption. Reframe the same buyer demand as decision-stage education ("How to choose…", "What every home bar needs") timed to the window, with a price-on-request / LINE CTA.
- Buddhist holy / sales-ban days — secular AND non-commercial. Anything publishing on those dates: no product push, no price, no "buy," and no reference to Buddhism or the religious reason. Reframe to a secular mindful / non-alcoholic / wellness angle, timed to the natural demand spike.
- Magento platform rule — no emoji. The blog does not render emoji. All published Title and Content TH/EN fields are plain text only — use "-" bullets, never emoji. (Emoji are fine in internal Notion-only fields, never in published content.)
### 15.7 Step 5 — Council QA + live verification
- Run the full §12 checklist on the finished drafts.
- Resolve every [VERIFY] — brand names, tasting notes, winery/bar names, ABV, prices, scores, pairings — via live research before publish. If a claim can't be confirmed, cut it or keep it flagged and hold the row. Never publish an unverified factual specific (§8).
### 15.8 Step 6 — Hero expansion
Expand each Hero from its v1 skeleton to full Word Target (§5), with sourcing and the repurpose tree (§13). Schedule this as its own work block — do not pass a skeleton off as a finished Hero.
### 15.9 Step 7 — Date re-flow & calendar QA
Once the row set is final, re-flow Publish Dates: even 2–3/day, 1 WN + 1 LIQ9 where possible, timely pieces pinned, weekends lighter, no two similar pieces adjacent. Build the filtered views (WN / LIQ9 / All-by-week) for the team.
### 15.10 Step 8 — Handoff & Definition of Done
Per §14, plus: internal hub-spoke links wired (Final URL), schema + images attached, repurpose tree logged, Status → Done → scheduled → Published.
### Month-build quick checklist
- [ ] Parameters locked (volume / data / focus)
- [ ] Live signals pulled; sales-ban dates confirmed & pinned
- [ ] 6–8 clusters designed; hub-spoke mapped; ~50/50 brand split
- [ ] Council pre-flight on the plan + owner sign-off
- [ ] New month DB created (schema mirrored; Month option added)
- [ ] Rows built: metadata + brief + bilingual v1 at Review
- [ ] Compliance applied (sale-naming, holy-day, no-emoji)
- [ ] Council QA done; every [VERIFY] resolved
- [ ] Heroes expanded + repurpose trees logged
- [ ] Dates re-flowed; team views built
- [ ] Handoff complete (links, schema, images, Final URL)

# PART C — BRAND DIRECTION BY SITE
> Expands §2. Read alongside §2 (voices) and §3 (E-E-A-T).
## 16. Wine-Now — direction
Positioning: Bangkok's sommelier, in your pocket. Premium = quality + fit, never status.
Audience: Thai urban professionals 28–50 getting into wine (TH-first); expats & connoisseurs (EN); gift buyers.
Promise: advice from a knowledgeable friend who happens to be a sommelier — we narrow the choice, we don't upsell.
Voice mechanics: Thai-first magazine warmth; calm authority; never academic, never breathless. No hyperbole — be sensory-specific. Never "drink this" — always why this bottle, this moment, this table. We say no; we explain (story, not spec sheet); we remember the reader (LINE OA); we're Thai.
Lexicon — lean in: pairing, structure, acidity, body, occasion, value, progression, "for your table," serving temperature.
Avoid: "best ever," "amazing," "deal," "cheap," "must-buy," status language, hard sell.
Categories WN owns: Education · Pairing (Thai food first — som tam, seafood, street food) · Spotlights (producers, Thai wine / New Latitude) · Travel (Khao Yai wine country, Bangkok wine bars) · Tips.
Default funnel: TOFU/MOFU education that leads to a LINE consult.
CTA pattern: "Ask the Wine-Now sommelier desk on LINE" · price-on-request · responsible drinking, 20+.
Sample line (EN): "Rainy-season humidity makes big reds feel heavier — reach for a chilled, high-acid white instead."
Wine-Now is NOT: a supermarket, a wine school, or "premium for status."
## 17. LIQ9 — direction
Positioning: the spirits intelligence behind Bangkok's bar scene.
Audience: cocktail-curious 25–45; home bartenders; the bar/hospitality crowd; gifting.
Promise: the witty insider who decodes the bar for you — confident, never gatekeeping.
Voice mechanics: Master-of-Malt wit + Bangkok-bartender confidence. Short-sentence punch; em-dash rhythm; insider language; self-aware humour. Decode, don't lecture. Cocktail-culture lens always present. Name real Bangkok bars / bartenders (e.g. Bar Us, Dry Wave, BKK Social Club, Vesper).
Lexicon — lean in: build, stir/shake, neat, on the rocks, highball, agave, dram, garnish, "behind the bar."
Avoid: bro-y excess, fake scarcity, lecture tone, jargon with no payoff.
Categories LIQ9 owns: Education · Recipes (with Recipe schema) · Spotlights (Thai hero spirits) · Travel (Bangkok cocktail bars) · Tips.
Thai hero spirits (verified): Iron Balls Gin (Bangkok — lemongrass, ginger, coconut-pineapple base) · Chalong Bay rum (Phuket — agricole, 100% first-press cane juice). Always confirm current tasting notes before publishing.
CTA pattern: "Ask the LIQ9 bartender desk on LINE" · price-on-request · drink mindfully, 20+.
Sample line (EN): "Forget the shot-and-lime — a good 100% agave tequila is built for sipping, slowly."
LIQ9 is NOT: a Wishbeer-style list, a duty-free, an importer, or whisky-only.

# PART D — CROSS-BRAND & PLATFORM RULES
## 18. Shared rules (both sites)
- The friend test (universal §2): every piece must read like advice from a brilliant, knowledgeable friend — not a salesperson, professor, or algorithm.
- TH + EN are two native voices, not translations (§10).
- Compliance is a hard gate every time (§9 + §15.6): no on-page price, LINE CTA, 20+, sales-ban-day rules, sale-naming rules.
- No fabricated facts — every score/claim sourced or "house description" (§8); resolve [VERIFY] before publish.
- Plain text only in published fields — no emoji in Title / Content TH / Content EN (Magento, §15.6).
- Hub-and-spoke linking within and across months (§6, §15.3).
- Author + bio + credentials + Person schema on every published piece (§3).

---
## §18 Process Additions — June 2026
### §18.1 Definition of Ready (DoR) — Pre-Handoff Gate
A piece may advance Review → Approved only when ALL below are confirmed:
1. All [VERIFY] tags resolved with a cited, live-sourced fact (no unresolved placeholders)
2. Internal links specified — each piece must name at least 2 target Brief IDs it links to (from the Master Topic Ledger)
3. Meta title (TH + EN) written — max 60 characters, includes primary keyword
4. Meta description (TH + EN) written — 140–160 characters, includes CTA
5. Image brief: at least one image described (shot list item, stock photo direction, or URL)
6. Schema type identified: Article / HowTo / FAQPage / Product / none
7. §9 Compliance gate passed (see §18.2 checklist)
8. Word count met: Hero/Pillar ≥ 2,500 words | Blog ≥ 800 words | Social ≥ 150 words
9. MOFU/BOFU pieces: destination specified — which category or product page does this link to?
No piece ships without all 9 checked. Reviewer initials the Notion checklist property.
### §18.2 §9 Compliance Checklist (expanded)
- [ ] No on-page price (no ฿ or THB + number in body copy or title)
- [ ] LINE CTA present (not a direct purchase link)
- [ ] 20+ age notice visible in Thai-language content
- [ ] If Publish Date is a Buddhist sales-ban day (Makha Bucha, Visakha Bucha, Asalha Bucha, Khao Phansa, Ok Phansa, and all wan phra in month): topic must be non-commercial, non-alcoholic focus, or secular framing — no buy-CTA, no product recommendation, no price
- [ ] Zero emoji characters in: Title (TH), Title (EN), Content TH, Content EN — Magento CMS rule
- [ ] No brand sale naming (§15.6 rule)
- [ ] Holy-day pieces: confirm secular + non-commercial + non-religious framing
### §18.3 Monthly Funnel Quota
- TOFU: maximum 70% of total pieces
- MOFU: minimum 20% of total pieces
- BOFU: minimum 10% of total pieces
BOFU pieces must link directly to a Magento product category page or specific product URL. Plans >70% TOFU must be revised before brief writing begins.
### §18.4 Hero / Pillar Word-Count Standard
Hero priority pieces (Pillar type) minimum word count is 2,500 words for combined TH + EN content. Drafts under 2,500 words must be expanded before Approved status. 1,700-word Pillar drafts are insufficient — this has been the recurring gap. Depth, not length, is the goal; the word count is a proxy for covering the topic completely.
